cases.input: What happens if DNS propagation times out?
cases.reply: If DNS propagation does not complete within the timeout, the change is to be treated as failed, and a rollback is executed in reverse order. Partial propagation can result in users being split across primary and DR sites. The prerequisite for the DNS update is to have the application re-pointed, DNS TTL verified at 60 seconds, and NetOps on bridge for coordination [DR-FIN-001 v3.2 section 6.2].

cases.input: What must the business owner confirm before the drill can be declared successful?
cases.reply: Before the drill can be declared successful, the business owner must confirm that the critical Finance workflow works at the DR site. Specifically, the Finance business owner must confirm the critical month-end posting workflow. The application must first be validated. The service should not be declared recovered if the business cannot operate. Additionally, the drill may be declared successful only when all mandatory steps, validations, and the business sign-off are complete [DR-FIN-001 v3.2 section 8.1; DR-POL-001 v2.0 section 3].

cases.input: What should we do if no usable recovery point can be confirmed?
cases.reply: If no usable recovery point can be confirmed, the procedure is to stop recovery, record the recovery point objective (RPO) as not measured, and escalate the issue to the Backup and Storage owner. It is important not to estimate the recovery point in this scenario [SOP-BKP-004 v1.6 section 2].

cases.input: In what order does rollback run?
cases.reply: Rollback runs in the reverse of the order in which actions were applied: DNS first, then application configuration, then database [DEP-FIN-001 v1.2 section 2].

cases.input: Does saying 'looks good' count as approval?
cases.reply: Saying "looks good" does not count as approval. Every state-changing recovery action requires explicit approval from the drill coordinator, and ambiguous replies such as "looks good" are not approval [DR-POL-001 v2.0 section 2].

cases.input: How do we undo the database failover?
cases.reply:
To undo the database failover in this drill, follow this rollback order as per the dependency map: 

1. Restore the DNS record to the primary load balancer. Expected result: DNS resolves to primary. Validation: simulated DNS state is primary. If it fails, escalate to NetOps and DR Lead [DR-FIN-001 v3.2 section 7.3, DEP-FIN-001 v1.2 section 2].

2. Restore the primary application configuration profile so the application points to the primary database. Validation: simulated application state is pointing_to_primary. If it fails, escalate to App Lead and DR Lead [DR-FIN-001 v3.2 section 7.2, DEP-FIN-001 v1.2 section 2].

3. Demote the DR database back to standby. Expected result: database returns to standby. Validation: simulated database state is standby. If it fails, escalate to DB Lead and DR Lead [DR-FIN-001 v3.2 section 7.1, DEP-FIN-001 v1.2 section 2].

This sequence safely rolls back from the DR state to the normal primary site state.
